articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor accidentally published AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's their personal diary. The agency tasked with protecting America's cyber infrastructure just leaked its own crown jewels to the internet.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: Palo Alto's PAN-OS GlobalProtect has an auth bypass vulnerability under active exploitation. Because nothing says 'global protect' like letting attackers waltz right past your authentication.

articles.title: Microsoft Threatens Researcher Over Bug Reports, Triggers Cybersecurity Uproar
articles.summary: Disgruntled researcher threatens to drop six zero-days after Microsoft 'humiliated' them and called the cops. Sometimes the house always wins, except when it doesn't.

articles.title: Zscaler Stock Plunges on Weak Guidance. Investors Were Maybe Right to Worry About an AI Apocalypse.
articles.summary: Microsoft threatens legal action against researcher for exposing Windows bugs, triggering cybersecurity community uproar. Nothing screams 'we care about security' like siccing lawyers on bug hunters.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: Critical RCE bug in open-source Git service Gogs remains unfixed since March, exploit module now available. Maintainers went full ghost mode while the vulnerability goes full public.

articles.title: Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw to Deploy Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Critical 9.4 CVSS vulnerability in Gogs allows authenticated users to execute arbitrary code. Self-hosted Git service becomes self-pwned Git service with one simple trick.

articles.title: Critical Gogs RCE Vulnerability Lets Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code
articles.summary: Hackers exploiting FortiClient EMS auth bypass to push EKZ infostealer malware. Enterprise management server becomes enterprise pwning server courtesy of CVE-2026-35616.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach, California AG claims they downplayed the mega-leak while paying ransom. Your genetic privacy sold separately, apparently.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification creates a privacy and security nightmare for everyone in lawmakers' rush to protect kids online. Digital ID requirements: because nothing protects children like surveilling everyone.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: License plate readers now used for school residency verification and noise complaints, because mission creep is the only mission that never fails. ALPR surveillance: not just for actual crimes anymore.
